Question Paper  
Exam Date & Time: 24-Dec-2025 (09:30 AM - 12:30 PM)  
  
  
  MANIPAL ACADEMY OF HIGHER EDUCATION  
  MANIPAL INSTITUTE OF TECHNOLOGY - BENGALURU  
  FIRST SEMESTER M.TECH. DEGREE MAKEUP EXAMINATION - DECEMBER 2025  
  Data Structures and Algorithms [CSS_5114]  
Marks: 50                                                                                                  Duration: 180 mins.  
  
  PART-A  
Answer all the questions.  
  
1)                Consider the following sequence of insertions into an AVL tree:                                       (5)  
  80, 60, 90, 50, 100, 40, 120, 30, 70, 110  
  A)           Draw the AVL tree after each insertion and show the required rotations.  
  Explain the balance factor after each insertion and rotation.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  B)           Implement a queue using two stacks. Perform the following operations:                                 (3)  
  
  Enqueue the values: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25.  
  Dequeue twice and then Enqueue: 30, 35, 40.  
  
  Dequeue two more values and show the final state of the queue.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO2" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  C)           Define an array of 5 student structures where each structure contains name (string), roll number (2)  
  (integer), and marks (integer array of size 3).  
  Write a program to calculate the average marks of all students using pointers.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
2)                Convert the following infix expression to postfix:                                                    (5)  
  (A + B) * (C - D) / (E + F) - (G + H)  
  A)  
  Show all the steps involved in the conversion using a stack.  
  
  Explain how to handle the operators and parentheses during the conversion process.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO2" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  B)           Write an algorithm to check if the following expression has balanced parentheses:                     (3)  
  {[(a + b) * (c / d)] - (e + f)}  
  Show the step-by-step execution of the algorithm with an explanation of how the stack is used to  
  match the parentheses.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO2" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  C)           Define a structure for a book containing title, author, and publisher.                                (2)  
  Inside the book structure, define another structure for publisher details containing name and  
  address.  
  
  Page #1

Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
3)        Sort the following list using Merge Sort:                                                          (5)  
  88, 12, 25, 34, 55, 15, 62, 90, 53, 73  
  A)   Show the recursive splitting and merging process. Write a function to perform the merge operation.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO1" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  B)   Implement Binary Search for element 42 in the sorted array:                                          (3)  
  $$arr[10] = {12, 14, 25, 32, 36, 42, 55, 66, 72, 88}$$  
  Develop the same with iterative method  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO1" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  C)   Given the graph with edges:                                                                          (2)  
  $$A → B = 3, B → C = 5, C → D = 2, D → A = 4$$  
  Compute the total weight of the edges and check if the graph is connected.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO5" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
4)        Given the following graph with nodes and weighted edges:                                             (5)  
  
  
  A)  
  
  
  Find the Minimum Spanning Tree (MST) of the given graph using Kruskal's Algorithm.  
  
  Show the steps involved in constructing the MST, including the edges chosen and their  
  weights.  
  
  Explain how the algorithm works step-by-step.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO5" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  B)   Create a circular linked list and perform the following operations:                                  (3)  
  Insert nodes with values: 10, 20, 30, 40, 50.  
  
  Insert a node at the beginning, at the end, and at position 3.  
  Display the final list after the operations.  
  
  Develop the code for the same.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  C)   Analyze the time complexity of the following code snippet using Big O notation:                      (2)  
  
  
  Page #2

$$for(i = 0; i <n; i++)$$  
$$for(j = 0; j < nz j++)$$  
$$for(k = j; k < n; k++)$$  
printt("tad", i+ j+ k);  
Course Outcome: "CO3"/ Cognitive Level: "Application"  
5) Given the infix expression: A + (B * C) - (D/E). (5)  
construct the corresponding expression tree.  
A) Explain each step in the construction of the tree. Construct  
In-order, pre-order and post-order traversals on the same.  
Replace A=9, B=3, C=2, D=4, E =1. Compute the equivalent  
value of expression using post-order traversal.  
Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
B) Sort the following array using the Bubble Sort algorithm: (3)  
10, 7, 8, 9, 1, 5, 3, 4,6  
Show the array after each pass of the algorithm.  
Course Outcome: "CO1"/ Cognitive Level: "Application"  
C) Given the following binary tree: (2)  
Convert this tree into a Binary Search Tree (BST) and  
explain the conversion process.  
Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Application"
